reasons.rubric: Enrolment status plus same-person binding is a multi-source match with a fragmented issuer ecosystem (many universities), so it needs design.
reasons.validity: Student fares are real, but operators accept a card photo today and the stated same-person link adds little to the fare decision.
reasons.coherence: The binding of student status to a payment account is stretched; a fare discount needs only the enrolment boolean.
reasons.novelty: Enrolled-student proof is already in the scholarship case; only the transit verifier is new.
reasons.provenance: The borrowed no-copy and photo-capture patterns are background colour and the idea reads the same without them.
reasons.retention_law: Transit operators have no obvious duty to keep a full ID copy, so retention law looks permissive rather than blocking.
reasons.linkability: A per-semester credential presented to one operator is linkable via the account binding, but this is tolerable.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Universities issuing per-semester wallet credentials to transit use is plausible but not an existing programme.
reasons.no_wallet: Needs the operator app to verify wallet proofs and students to hold a wallet, which is not yet common.

reasons.rubric: One-person-one-account via telco is a nullifier use with a fragmented issuer set (three telcos) and a person-versus-line key problem, so it needs design.
reasons.validity: Scalper bots at concert presales are a real Taiwanese problem and uniqueness per event does address it if the telco can sign a per-person claim.
reasons.coherence: Event-scoped nullifier and per-person telco claim fit, though the telco being in the loop undercuts the privacy goal.
reasons.novelty: Sybil resistance is already catalogued for brokerage accounts; the new parts are the telco issuer and the ticketing moment.
reasons.provenance: The ID-copy pattern is loosely relevant, while the sealed-bid source is only a metaphor for event scoping and adds nothing.
reasons.retention_law: A ticketing platform has no obvious legal duty to retain full ID, so retention law holds as a non-blocker.
reasons.linkability: Cross-event unlinkability is the explicit design goal, though a telco issuing in advance may see participation.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Telcos would need to build a per-person uniqueness attestation with no business incentive, which is a serious barrier.
reasons.no_wallet: Fans need a wallet and the ticketer must verify proofs; adoption for a one-off presale is unlikely without platform mandate.

reasons.rubric: Membership in a utility-signed roll is a clean predicate, but frequency is low and the roll may not exist, so it is a weak fit.
reasons.validity: Vulnerable-household lists collected by volunteers are a real risk, but responders need the address for dispatch so the benefit is limited to enrolment.
reasons.coherence: The proof helps enrolment checks only, and the idea honestly says it does not help dispatch, so the parts fit but the benefit is narrow.
reasons.novelty: Nothing on the known list touches medical-equipment dependence or disaster response.
reasons.retention_law: The verifiers are volunteers and offices with no clear duty to hold full records, though public agencies may have record rules I cannot confirm.
reasons.linkability: A membership proof to a small set of volunteers is low risk, but a small roll makes anonymity sets tiny.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: The utility would have to create and sign a medical-need roll it may not keep, which is uncertain.
reasons.no_wallet: The households in question are elderly and ill, who are least likely to hold or use a wallet.

reasons.rubric: Same-person match across two issuers with private landlords as verifiers is a low-adoption multi-source match, so it is a weak fit.
reasons.validity: Landlords do collect ID copies, but a landlord needs to know who is on the lease, so hiding the ID number conflicts with the decision.
reasons.coherence: The lease moment, rent subsidy claim and ID-number concealment pull in different directions, since the lease itself names the tenant.
reasons.novelty: Renting and student enrolment are both on the known list, so this is mostly a recombination.
reasons.provenance: The borrowed discretionary-copy and deletion-exception points describe the problem but do not shape the proposed mechanism.
reasons.retention_law: Private landlords have no stated duty to retain, but a subsidy administrator may require full documents, which is unknown.
reasons.linkability: Landlord and university are single parties, so linkability is not a major problem.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Household registration offices signing a match credential for landlord use is unlikely without a mandate.
reasons.no_wallet: Small landlords will not run verifier software, as the idea itself concedes.

reasons.rubric: A freshness boolean on employment is simple, but employers are a fragmented issuer set and the verifier still wants a name, so it needs design.
reasons.validity: Rent and deposit checks do ask for employment proof in Taiwan and a current-employment boolean is mostly sufficient.
reasons.coherence: Short-lived revocable status fits the stale-certificate problem well, with the name caveat honestly noted.
reasons.novelty: Income and employment proof appears in the loan case, but employment status for a rental renewal is a new predicate on a familiar moment.
reasons.provenance: The purpose-limitation and field-selection borrowings are generic and the design would read the same without them.
reasons.retention_law: A landlord has no apparent duty to retain the full certificate, so this holds.
reasons.linkability: Weekly refreshed proofs from one employer could link the holder across presentations unless unlinkable proofs are used.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Employers can sign easily at large firms, but small employers with no HR system are unlikely issuers and may not want revocation duties.
reasons.no_wallet: Landlords and tenants would need wallet tooling, and a LINE photo of a certificate is far easier.

reasons.rubric: A coded category with an expiry is a simple attribute, but it needs agreed codes across hospitals and schools, so it is a design-needed fit.
reasons.validity: Schools and employers do receive diagnoses where a category and end date would suffice, and a hospital can plausibly sign it.
reasons.coherence: The category plus auto-expiry addresses the over-disclosure and indefinite-retention problems directly.
reasons.novelty: Health accommodations for schools and employers are untouched by the known list.
reasons.provenance: The differential privacy and permanent-number sources are only loose analogies and nothing in the idea depends on them.
reasons.retention_law: Schools may have record-keeping rules for health documents, which I cannot confirm.
reasons.linkability: A category claim from a few hospitals to one school is low risk, but rare categories could still identify the child.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Hospitals have liability concerns and no incentive to build per-category attestations, which makes this a real barrier.
reasons.no_wallet: Parents would need a wallet and the school health office a verifier, and teachers still prefer a conversation.

reasons.rubric: A threshold on rating and trip count is simple, but the issuer is an unwilling platform scraped via zkTLS, so it is a weak fit.
reasons.validity: Deposit waiver is a real moment, but a ride-hail rating says little about driving risk and the operator still needs a license check.
reasons.coherence: The predicate does not match what the operator is actually trying to decide, which is driving and damage risk.
reasons.novelty: No known case touches reputation transfer between platforms.
reasons.provenance: The one-bit proof and whole-document-capture ideas are generic and the design reads the same without them.
reasons.retention_law: Rental operators have no obvious duty to retain the account screenshot, but they do retain licenses.
reasons.linkability: A zkTLS proof reveals nothing beyond the threshold, but the platform sees the session and could link it.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: The platform has not agreed and its terms may forbid this use, and the idea concedes this.
reasons.no_wallet: Needs a zkTLS prover in the traveller's app and a verifier at the kiosk, which does not exist.

reasons.rubric: An average-balance threshold is a range-type predicate from a single bank among many, and a weaker substitute for cheques, so it is a weak fit.
reasons.validity: Instalment plans exist, but schools mostly use post-dated cheques or card billing, and a one-bank balance may not be accepted as sufficient.
reasons.coherence: The predicate and verifier fit together, though the one-bank scope undercuts reliability as the idea admits.
reasons.novelty: Bank balance proof is close to the loan income case, though the school tuition moment is new.
reasons.retention_law: Private schools have no obvious duty to retain statements, so this holds.
reasons.linkability: A bank signing a balance statistic to a school is low linkability risk.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Banks are used to issuing statements but may not want to sign statistics as a new product.
reasons.no_wallet: Parents and small cram schools would need wallet tooling for a low-stakes check, which is unlikely.
